<!-- Handpan Studio bridge for masterthehandpan.com — build 2026-09-26a.
     Paste ONCE into Site settings -> Custom code -> Footer code (or a page's
     "before </body>" code). It does nothing on a page without the #hps-app
     iframe, so it is safe site-wide. Finds the lesson's Vimeo player through
     Vimeo's Player SDK (loaded only when a Vimeo iframe is on the page) and
     feeds its clock to the app in the iframe. The Wistia loader is left out:
     this site has no Wistia.
     2026-09-21a: the app can MUTE and UNMUTE the lesson video (the tour turns the video's sound on when it
     starts), and the bridge says it can in its status message - an older bridge would take an unknown
     command for a pause, so the app asks only a bridge that has said so. The same build sets the video's
     PLAYBACK SPEED on request (action "rate", with rate 0.25-2), for the tour to use.
     2026-09-25a: FULL SCREEN ON A PHONE THAT HAS NONE (the iPhone): the app asks this page to pin its frame over the
     whole window and to put it back, and the bridge says "fs" in its status - an older app never asks.
     2026-09-26a: ON A PHONE THE FRAME RUNS EDGE TO EDGE - measured, so the page never scrolls sideways. -->
<script>
(function(){
  /* Handpan Studio bridge — build 2026-09-26a (Vimeo, muted derived; mute, unmute and speed on request). Kept INSIDE the script so it
     travels when only this block is re-pasted (the iframe above carries the
     piece and its tempo map in the URL and must not be replaced). */
  function frame(){ return document.getElementById('hps-app'); }
  function send(m){ var f=frame(); if(f&&f.contentWindow) try{ f.contentWindow.postMessage(m,'*'); }catch(e){} }
  /* SPACE PLAYS AND STOPS THE APP FROM THE LESSON PAGE (build 2026-09-02a).
     Keys go to whatever has focus, and on a lesson page that is Kajabi's own
     document until the student has clicked inside the app — where a bare
     space only scrolls the page. Forwarded to the app, which answers with
     its transport. Not while typing in a field, never with a modifier. */
  document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){
    if(e.key!==' '||e.metaKey||e.ctrlKey||e.altKey) return;
    var t=e.target, tag=t&&t.tagName;
    if(tag==='INPUT'||tag==='TEXTAREA'||tag==='SELECT'||(t&&t.isContentEditable)) return;
    if(!frame()) return;
    e.preventDefault(); send({type:'hps-key',key:' '});
  });
  /* THE CLOCK GOES OUT TWICE OVER, AND THE SECOND WAY ONLY SPEAKS WHEN THE
     FIRST HAS GONE QUIET. requestAnimationFrame gives the tight anchor; a
     timer gives a floor under it, because rAF does not merely slow when the
     page stops being composited, it STOPS. sendTime stamps every report, so
     the heartbeat stays silent while frames are flowing. */
  var lastSend=0, pumping=false;
  /* AND WHETHER THE PLAYER'S OWN SOUND IS ON (David, 28 Aug: the app "should go
     mute when audio is switched back on in the video player"). Read off the
     real <video> element, which is reachable for both players — that is how the
     duplicate pump used to find Wistia's own element — so muted-or-silent is
     one flag either way, and Wistia's mutechange/volumechange are bound below
     as a cross-check. */
  function vmuted(el){
    if(!el) return null;
    return !!(el.muted||el.volume===0);
  }
  /* p — IS THE VIDEO PLAYING, stated, not left for the app to guess. The app
     used to infer a pause from the clock standing still, and a muted video
     scrolled out of view stands still in exactly the same way: browsers
     throttle what nobody can see or hear, so its clock moves in coarse jumps
     the inference kept mistaking for a stop (David, 28 Aug, three times).
     The player knows the truth; send it with every report. */
  function sendTime(t,r,m,p){ lastSend=Date.now();
    var msg={type:'hps-video-time',t:t,r:r};
    if(m!=null) msg.m=m;
    if(p!=null) msg.p=!!p;
    send(msg); }
  function heartbeat(read){ setInterval(function(){
    if(Date.now()-lastSend>150) try{ read(); }catch(e){} },150); }
  function status(st){ send({type:'hps-bridge',status:st,can:['sound','rate','fs']}); }
  var found=false, sIv=setInterval(function(){ status(found?'connected':'searching'); },1000);
  /* The app schedules the pan against the AUDIO clock, so it must know how
     fast the video's clock is running — at 0.5x an offset alone put every
     stroke twice too early. Every timecode now carries r. The app can also
     measure the rate itself, so an old un-repasted block still works; this
     just makes the change instant and exact. */
  // the app's play button (in follow mode) toggles whichever player we found
  var ctl=null;
  /* THE VIDEO'S SOUND, ON THE APP'S REQUEST (David, 21 Sep 2026: "make sure the video is unmuted when the tour
     starts" … "also add mute as a function"). snd(true) unmutes - and lifts a volume left at 0, which mutes as
     surely - snd(false) mutes. Set by whichever player was found. */
  var snd=null;
  /* …and its playback speed (David, 21 Sep: "can we also control the playback speed of the video?"): spd(r) with r
     between 0.25 and 2, the range the players offer */
  var spd=null;
  /* FULL SCREEN ON A PHONE THAT HAS NONE (David, 25 Sep 2026). The frame's own style attribute is kept and put back
     exactly; while pinned the page does not scroll under it, and a height the app asks for is kept for afterwards. */
  var pinned=false, pinSaved=null, pinH=0;
  function pin(on){
    var f=frame(); if(!f||on===pinned) return; pinned=on;
    var de=document.documentElement, b=document.body;
    if(on){
      pinSaved={st:f.getAttribute('style')||'', de:de.style.overflow, b:b.style.overflow}; pinH=0;
      f.style.cssText=pinSaved.st+';position:fixed;left:0;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;width:100vw;height:100vh;height:100dvh;'
        +'max-width:none;margin:0;border-radius:0;z-index:2147483647';
      de.style.overflow='hidden'; b.style.overflow='hidden';
    } else {
      f.setAttribute('style',pinSaved.st); de.style.overflow=pinSaved.de; b.style.overflow=pinSaved.b;
      if(pinH) f.style.height=pinH+'px';
      bleed();
    }
  }
  /* THE FRAME RUNS EDGE TO EDGE ON A PHONE (David, 26 Sep 2026 - build 2026-09-26a). Measured, never assumed: the frame
     is pulled out to the screen's left edge by exactly its distance from it and made as wide as the screen, so an
     uneven column cannot push it past the edge and the page never scrolls sideways; a wider screen gets the frame's own
     style back. Not while pinned - full screen owns the frame then, and letting go measures again. */
  var bleedOrig=null, bleedT=0;
  function bleed(){
    var f=frame(); if(!f||pinned) return;
    if(!bleedOrig) bleedOrig={w:f.style.width,r:f.style.borderRadius,m:f.style.marginLeft,x:f.style.maxWidth};
    f.style.width=bleedOrig.w; f.style.borderRadius=bleedOrig.r; f.style.marginLeft=bleedOrig.m; f.style.maxWidth=bleedOrig.x;
    if(window.innerWidth>600) return;
    var r=f.getBoundingClientRect(), vw=document.documentElement.clientWidth, m0=parseFloat(getComputedStyle(f).marginLeft)||0;
    f.style.marginLeft=(m0-r.left)+'px'; f.style.width=vw+'px'; f.style.maxWidth='none'; f.style.borderRadius='0';
  }
  function bleedSoon(){ clearTimeout(bleedT); bleedT=setTimeout(bleed,60); }
  bleed();
  window.addEventListener('resize',bleedSoon);
  window.addEventListener('orientationchange',bleedSoon);
  window.addEventListener('load',bleed);
  window.addEventListener('message',function(e){
    var d=e.data;
    if(d&&d.type==='hps-video-ctl'&&(d.action==='mute'||d.action==='unmute')){ if(snd) try{ snd(d.action==='unmute'); }catch(err){} return; }
    if(d&&d.type==='hps-video-ctl'&&d.action==='rate'){ var r=+d.rate; if(spd&&r>=0.25&&r<=2) try{ spd(r); }catch(err){} return; }
    if(d&&d.type==='hps-video-ctl'&&ctl){ try{ ctl(d.action||'toggle',d.t); }catch(err){} return; }
    /* THE APP ASKS FOR THE HEIGHT IT NEEDS (David, 28 Aug: "extend the
       available window to full player size and then lock vertical scrolling").
       It knows what its notation comes to and a fixed 820px did not — so the
       window follows the music rather than the music being shrunk to the
       window. Bounded either side: a silly number from anywhere is ignored,
       and only this page's own frame is touched. */
    if(d&&d.type==='hps-fs'){ var ff=frame(); if(ff&&e.source===ff.contentWindow) pin(!!d.on); return; }
    if(d&&d.type==='hps-size'&&typeof d.h==='number'&&d.h>300&&d.h<4000){
      if(pinned){ pinH=Math.round(d.h); return; }
      var f=frame(); if(f) f.style.height=Math.round(d.h)+'px';
    }
  });
  // 1) Wistia — E-v1.js above also upgrades Wistia IFRAME embeds into API handles
  window._wq=window._wq||[];
  /* THE CAUSE OF "PLAYBACK STOPS WHEN I SCROLL DOWN" (28 Aug, David's third
     report — and his observation that video-sound-on was immune cracked it):
     Wistia DELIBERATELY PAUSES a muted video the moment it scrolls fully out
     of view, and resumes it when it returns. Documented, default true, named
     playSuspendedOffScreen. The pan follows the video, so the pan stopped at
     an exact scroll line and restarted a few px back up — the app was
     faithfully following a video that really was pausing. Asked off here;
     this push only takes effect if it lands before Wistia embeds, so the
     onReady guard below covers the race the other way. */
  _wq.push({id:'_all',options:{playSuspendedOffScreen:false}});
  _wq.push({id:'_all',onReady:function(v){
    /* ONE PUMP ONLY. id:'_all' fires for every Wistia player on the page and
       can fire again when one re-initialises, and the <video> hunt below finds
       Wistia's own <video> element — so without this the same player was
       pumped twice over (counted: two loops from one video). */
    if(pumping) return;
    pumping=true; clearInterval(iv);
    found=true; status('connected');
    var askedPause=false;   // a pause the STUDENT chose, via the app's button
    ctl=function(a,t){
      if(a==='seek'&&t!=null){ v.time(t); return; }
      var playing=v.state()==='playing';
      if(a==='play'||(a==='toggle'&&!playing)){ askedPause=false; v.play(); }
      else { askedPause=true; v.pause(); } };
    snd=function(on){ if(on){ v.unmute(); if(v.volume&&v.volume()===0) v.volume(1); } else v.mute(); };
    spd=function(r){ v.playbackRate(r); };
    /* If the options push above lost the race to the embed, Wistia still
       suspends off-screen — so any pause that arrives while the player is
       FULLY out of view, and that neither the student's scrubbing nor the
       app's button asked for, is Wistia's own and is undone on the spot. A
       student cannot click pause on a player that is not on screen; the one
       off-screen pause they CAN cause goes through ctl and is honoured. */
    try{ v.bind('pause',function(){
      if(askedPause) return;
      var c=v.container||document.querySelector('.wistia_embed');
      if(!c) return;
      var r=c.getBoundingClientRect();
      if(r.bottom<=0||r.top>=window.innerHeight){ try{ v.play(); }catch(e){} }
    }); }catch(e){}
    try{ v.bind('play',function(){ askedPause=false; }); }catch(e){}
    // playbackRate() is documented as a SETTER only — calling it bare could
    // set the rate to undefined, so never read it. The event is the getter.
    /* THE RATE MUST BE READABLE AT ANY MOMENT, not only after the student has
       changed it. playbackRate() on the Wistia API is a documented SETTER, so
       it can never be read — the event was the only getter, which left wr
       sitting at 1 whenever a player opened at a remembered speed, and the app
       TRUSTS a stated rate over its own measurement. Wistia renders a real
       <video>, so read that element's live playbackRate and keep the event as
       the fallback. */
    var wr=1, wvid=null;
    try{ v.bind('playbackratechange',function(r){
      if(typeof r==='number'&&r>0.05&&r<8) wr=r; }); }catch(e){}
    function wel(){
      try{ if(!wvid||!wvid.isConnected) wvid=findVideo(document); }catch(e){}
      return wvid;
    }
    function wrate(){
      var r=wel()&&wvid.playbackRate;
      return (typeof r==='number'&&r>0.05&&r<8)?r:wr;
    }
    var wmute=null;                      // what Wistia's own events last said
    try{ v.bind('mutechange',function(x){ wmute=!!x; }); }catch(e){}
    try{ v.bind('volumechange',function(x){ if(typeof x==='number') wmute=(x===0); }); }catch(e){}
    function wmuted(){ var m=vmuted(wel()); return m==null?wmute:m; }
    // every frame for the anchor, and the heartbeat underneath it for the
    // states where frames stop coming
    (function pump(){ sendTime(v.time(),wrate(),wmuted(),v.state()==='playing'); requestAnimationFrame(pump); })();
    heartbeat(function(){ sendTime(v.time(),wrate(),wmuted(),v.state()==='playing'); });
  }});
  // 2) Vimeo — masterthehandpan.com (Webflow) hosts its lessons on Vimeo,
  //    whose player is a CROSS-ORIGIN iframe: the <video> hunt below cannot see
  //    into it, so the Player SDK is the only way to its clock. The SDK is
  //    loaded only once a Vimeo iframe is actually on the page, so a Kajabi
  //    lesson never fetches it. It attaches to any existing player iframe
  //    (Webflow's Video element makes one) or a data-vimeo-id element.
  function vimeoEl(){
    return document.querySelector('iframe[src*="player.vimeo.com"],[data-vimeo-id],[data-vimeo-url]');
  }
  var vimeoAsked=false;
  function vimeoSDK(){
    if(window.Vimeo&&window.Vimeo.Player) return true;
    if(!vimeoAsked){ vimeoAsked=true;
      var s=document.createElement('script'); s.src='https://player.vimeo.com/api/player.js'; s.async=true;
      document.head.appendChild(s); }
    return false;
  }
  function vimeoPump(el){
    var p=new Vimeo.Player(el);
    /* THE SDK ANSWERS BY PROMISE, not on the spot — every read is a round
       trip into the player's frame. So the state the app wants stated (rate,
       mute, playing) is kept here from the player's own events, and only the
       clock is asked for, one question in flight at a time: a frame that
       finds the last answer still out simply waits for it. Vimeo's own
       timeupdate fires ~4x a second, far too coarse for the follow engine
       (it drops notes below a handful of reports a second), which is why the
       clock is polled rather than listened for. */
    /* MUTED IS ONE DERIVED VALUE, never two sources writing one flag (David,
       2 Sep, Safari on the Webflow page: the "video sound is off/on" dialogs
       re-opened the instant they were closed and stacked two deep — the flag
       was flapping). The muted switch and the volume are tracked apart: the
       volumechange event only ever sets the volume, the getMuted poll only
       ever sets the switch, and what goes out is switch-on OR volume-zero. A
       volumechange reporting volume 1 while the switch is on — which is what
       a muted player says when its volume is asked — can no longer flip it. */
    var vt=0, vr=1, vmuteSw=null, vvol=null, vplay=false, inflight=false;
    function vmuted(){ if(vmuteSw==null&&vvol==null) return null; return !!(vmuteSw||vvol===0); }
    function report(){ sendTime(vt,vr,vmuted(),vplay); }
    function ask(){
      if(inflight) return; inflight=true;
      p.getCurrentTime().then(function(s){ inflight=false;
        if(typeof s==='number') vt=s; report(); },function(){ inflight=false; });
    }
    ctl=function(a,t){
      if(a==='seek'&&t!=null){ p.setCurrentTime(t); return; }
      if(a==='play'||(a==='toggle'&&!vplay)) p.play(); else p.pause(); };
    /* Vimeo answers with a promise, and a browser may refuse sound the viewer has not allowed: the state the app
       hears is set only when Vimeo says it happened */
    snd=function(on){
      p.setMuted(!on).then(function(){ vmuteSw=!on; report(); },function(){});
      if(on&&vvol===0) p.setVolume(1).then(function(){ vvol=1; report(); },function(){}); };
    spd=function(r){ p.setPlaybackRate(r).then(function(){ vr=r; report(); },function(){}); };
    p.on('play',function(){ vplay=true; report(); });
    p.on('pause',function(){ vplay=false; report(); });
    p.on('ended',function(){ vplay=false; report(); });
    p.on('seeked',function(d){ if(d&&typeof d.seconds==='number') vt=d.seconds; report(); });
    p.on('playbackratechange',function(d){ var r=d&&d.playbackRate;
      if(typeof r==='number'&&r>0.05&&r<8) vr=r; });
    p.on('volumechange',function(d){ if(d&&typeof d.volume==='number') vvol=d.volume; });
    /* muted is not an event in this SDK, so it is asked for on a slow tick,
       together with the values the events may have missed at attach time */
    function slow(){
      try{ p.getMuted().then(function(m){ vmuteSw=!!m; }); }catch(e){}
      try{ p.getVolume().then(function(v){ if(typeof v==='number') vvol=v; }); }catch(e){}
      try{ p.getPlaybackRate().then(function(r){ if(typeof r==='number'&&r>0.05&&r<8) vr=r; }); }catch(e){}
    }
    p.ready().then(function(){
      found=true; status('connected');
      p.getPaused().then(function(x){ vplay=!x; });
      slow(); setInterval(slow,500);
      (function pump(){ ask(); requestAnimationFrame(pump); })();
      heartbeat(ask);
    });
  }
  // 3) any <video> — page, same-origin iframes, and shadow roots
  function findVideo(root){
    var v=root.querySelector&&root.querySelector('video'); if(v) return v;
    var all=root.querySelectorAll?root.querySelectorAll('*'):[];
    for(var i=0;i<all.length;i++) if(all[i].shadowRoot){ var s=findVideo(all[i].shadowRoot); if(s) return s; }
    return null;
  }
  var tries=0, iv=setInterval(function(){
    if(pumping){ clearInterval(iv); return; }     // Wistia got there first
    var vel=vimeoEl();
    if(vel){ if(!vimeoSDK()){ if(++tries>40){ clearInterval(iv); clearInterval(sIv); status('no-player'); } return; }
      clearInterval(iv); pumping=true; vimeoPump(vel); return; }
    var vid=findVideo(document);
    if(!vid){ var ifr=document.querySelectorAll('iframe');
      for(var i=0;i<ifr.length&&!vid;i++){ try{ if(ifr[i].contentDocument) vid=findVideo(ifr[i].contentDocument); }catch(e){} } }
    if(vid){ clearInterval(iv); pumping=true; found=true; status('connected');
      ctl=function(a,t){
        if(a==='seek'&&t!=null){ vid.currentTime=t; return; }
        if(a==='play'||(a==='toggle'&&vid.paused)) vid.play&&vid.play(); else vid.pause&&vid.pause(); };
      snd=function(on){ vid.muted=!on; if(on&&vid.volume===0) vid.volume=1; };
      spd=function(r){ vid.playbackRate=r; };
      /* while paused the reports keep coming, carrying p:false — a pause the
         app hears about at once beats one it must deduce from silence */
      (function pump(){ sendTime(vid.currentTime,vid.playbackRate,vmuted(vid),!vid.paused);
        requestAnimationFrame(pump); })();
      heartbeat(function(){ sendTime(vid.currentTime,vid.playbackRate,vmuted(vid),!vid.paused); });
      vid.addEventListener('seeked',function(){
        sendTime(vid.currentTime,vid.playbackRate,vmuted(vid),!vid.paused); });
    } else if(++tries>40){ clearInterval(iv); clearInterval(sIv); status('no-player'); }
  },1000);
})();
</script>
